name: Electric Bicycle
description: A bicycle with fully operable pedals and an electric motor of fewer than 750 watts, with a top assisted speed of 28 mph or less, in one of three classes: Class 1 pedal assist to 20 mph, Class 2 throttle to 20 mph, and Class 3 pedal assist to 28 mph.

restrictions.rule: Fully operable pedals and an electric motor of fewer than 750 watts, with a top assisted speed of 28 mph or less (Texas Transportation Code §664.001)
Class 1 assists only while the rider pedals, to a top assisted speed of 20 mph (Texas Transportation Code §664.001)
Class 2 can be propelled by its motor without pedaling, to a top assisted speed of 20 mph (Texas Transportation Code §664.001)
Class 3 assists only while the rider pedals, to a top assisted speed of more than 20 but less than 28 mph, and must be sold with a speedometer (Texas Transportation Code §§664.001, 664.004)
May only be ridden if the motor disengages when the rider stops pedaling or applies the brakes (Texas Transportation Code §551.107)
Carries a permanent label stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage; anyone who changes its motor-powered speed or engagement must replace the label to match
Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements (16 CFR part 1512)
Class 3 riders must be 15 or older; a younger passenger may ride on one (Texas Transportation Code §551.107)
No driver's license, title or insurance, and it can't be registered for highway use (Texas Transportation Code §551.107)

TxDOT and local authorities may not ban it from roads used mainly by motor vehicles, or from anywhere a regular bicycle may go, except natural-surface trails closed to motor vehicles (Texas Transportation Code §551.106)
TxDOT and local authorities may ban bicycles, e-bikes included, from sidewalks and set speed limits on bicycle paths (Texas Transportation Code §551.106)
